transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-10-06
- Start: 16:00 PT
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Blake (Redwood SE), Rajat Singh (Aerolith Head of Search), Olivia Park (Aerolith Data Eng), Tom Greene (Aerolith CTO)

Summary (auto): Aerolith is reworking their search stack to add semantic reranking and embeddings for better recall. They currently use Elastic + custom BM25, considering Pinecone or FAISS-backed approach. Main drivers: improve relevance for long-tail queries, lower false negatives, and keep 99th percentile latency under 250ms for front-end results.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, this is Ethan our systems SE.
00:07 Speaker 2 (Rajat): Hey, Rajat here, I run search at Aerolith. Olivia and Tom are on from eng.
00:13 Speaker 1 (Maya): Great, high-level agenda: understand current infra, traffic and SLOs, discuss vector DB/integration options, and map Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for you.
00:24 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Hi all, I'll focus on the throughput, embedding dims, and rerank pipeline questions. Quick Q: do you already have embeddings — or are you planning to generate at index time?
00:32 Speaker 4 (Olivia): We're planning to generate embeddings at index time. Currently we use a 2-step pipeline: candidate retrieval via BM25 in Elastic then a re-ranker. Re-ranker is currently logistic regression-ish, we want to replace it with an embedding-based rerank (dense vector dot products + a small cross-encoder for top N).
00:48 Speaker 2 (Rajat): Volume: production has about 50M docs, mostly short docs but with a 10% set of long-form pages. Query load varies — baseline ~400 QPS, peak up to ~2k QPS during campaigns.
01:01 Speaker 3 (Ethan): That peak number is super helpful. For Hosted vs Dedicated, if you need 2k QPS consistently with sub-250ms tail latency, Dedicated or Private usually is the fit because of predictable GPU pools and reserved capacity. Hosted can work if you accept bursty cold starts and slightly higher 99th perc latency for some model choices.
01:18 Speaker 5 (Tom): Our security bar is SOC2 in place, but for some customers we need VPC/VPN and customer-managed KMS. Is Redwood Private something we should consider?
01:27 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes — Redwood Private gives a customer-managed control plane and KMS integrations; Dedicated is still multi-tenant control plane but isolated GPU pools. We'll send the SOC2 and VPC/KMS docs after.
01:36 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Technical: on dimensionality — are you targeting off-the-shelf model dims like 1536 (OpenAI ada??) or smaller 768? Lower dims save storage and index memory but can impact recall for some tasks.
01:48 Speaker 2 (Rajat): We tested both. 1536 vectors give marginally better MRR on long-tail queries, but memory overhead was substantial. Our ops prefer 768 for cost but we're worried about recall drop.
01:58 Speaker 3 (Ethan): We usually recommend trying a two-tier approach: store 768 for immediate candidate retrieval and keep 1536 for occasional rerank on hard queries, or use mixed precision quantized indexes. Also hybrid search is common — BM25 to get recall then dense rerank; or using HNSW on top of FAISS with IVF for large scales.
02:21 Speaker 4 (Olivia): About vector DBs — we're leaning to Pinecone because it's managed, but concerned about egress and per-index costs. We also evaluated Milvus and self-hosted FAISS.
02:31 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Right — tradeoffs: Pinecone/managed removes ops burden but costs can scale; Milvus/Weaviate give more control. FAISS self-hosted gives cheapest storage but you shoulder sharding/replication. Redwood can integrate with any — you can host embeddings in your DB and call Redwood's rerank/embedding endpoints or host the model on Dedicated to run nearest-neighbor locally.
02:48 Speaker 2 (Rajat): For rerank model, we expect to do a dot-product for top 50 then a cross-encoder over top 5. Are there recommendations for batch sizes?
02:58 Speaker 3 (Ethan): For dot-product scoring at high QPS, batch size and continuous batching matter. On Dedicated, we can tune batch sizes to maximize throughput: typical batch windows 20–50ms, batching up to 64-128 for GPUs depending on model; cross-encoder is more expensive so we recommend only doing that for top-K (K=5). Redwood's runtime supports dynamic batching and KV cache for chat-like flows; for rerank this is simpler but we still get gains from batching.
03:22 Speaker 4 (Olivia): What's the expected index size for 50M docs at 768 vs 1536 dims? Rough numbers to present to infra?
03:29 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Rough calc: 50M * 768 * 4 bytes ~ 153.6 GB uncompressed; at 1536 dims it's ~307GB. With PQ/IVF or 8-bit quantization you can cut that by 4x-8x. But be mindful of memory vs disk and HNSW graph overhead.
03:48 Speaker 5 (Tom): Latency SLOs: front-end needs 250ms 99th; backend async rerank can be 500–800ms. Is that achievable if we host embedding generation externally?
04:00 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Yes if the candidate retrieval is fast and rerank is limited to top 50 with efficient vector lookup. Dedicated provides predictable p99 for embeddings generation and dot-product scoring. Hosted could still meet p50 easily but p99 might be higher depending on region and multi-tenant load.
04:18 Speaker 2 (Rajat): Any gotchas with hybrid search? We worry about inconsistent scoring between BM25 and vector scores.
04:25 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Classic issue — score normalization and feature blending needed. Options: re-scale BM25 and vector scores or use a learning-to-rank model on top. Redwood clients often do a feature concat approach and train a downstream ranker. For quick wins, use BM25 for recall and rely on dense rerank to reorder top results.
04:45 Speaker 4 (Olivia): What about indexing latency for real-time updates? We have frequent content updates, need near real-time availability (seconds to a minute).
04:54 Speaker 3 (Ethan): For near real-time, consider a write-through approach: index to your primary store + async batch to vector index; for strong consistency you can do point upserts in the vector DB. Dedicated/private deployments can be tuned for fast upsert throughput; Pinecone has fast upserts too but cost varies.
05:08 Speaker 2 (Rajat): Ops question: backup/restore and disaster recovery for vector indexes?
05:14 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Backups depend on DB; FAISS self-hosted you control snapshots. Managed services typically offer snapshots and export. Redwood Private allows you to keep control of snapshots and KMS for encrypted backups. We'll include DR best practices in the notes.
05:27 Speaker 1 (Maya): Quick check — any regulatory or residency constraints?
05:31 Speaker 5 (Tom): Some EU customers require data to remain in EU regions and we need audit logs for model inference; SSO/SAML is a must.
05:38 Speaker 1 (Maya): Noted — Redwood supports per-region deployments and audit logs; SSO/SAML/SCIM can be configured. We'll attach security docs.
05:45 Speaker 2 (Rajat): Pricing question — what's the expected ballpark for Dedicated for our scale?
05:50 Speaker 1 (Maya): I'll send a tailored pricing sheet, but order-of-magnitude: if you need reserved capacity for 2k QPS steady rerank generation, you're looking at mid-five-figures to low-six-figures per month depending on model choices and replication. We'll break down unit economics (per-token, per-embedding, storage) in the estimate.
06:07 Speaker 4 (Olivia): For benchmarking, what would you need from us?
06:12 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Ideally: sample of ~10k queries that represent tail, head, and campaign traffic, sample documents (10k–100k rows) and the candidate retrieval output if available. We'll run both vector-only and hybrid rerank tests and provide MRR/latency/cost comparisons.
06:27 Speaker 2 (Rajat): Sounds good. One more — how do you handle fallbacks if Dedicated capacity is overwhelmed?
06:33 Speaker 3 (Ethan): Redwood supports routing policies and fallbacks: you can fallback to a cheaper model, region, or an older endpoint. For hybrid, you can also fallback to BM25-only results until capacity recovers.
06:48 Speaker 1 (Maya): Alright let's recap next steps. Ethan will share benchmark plan and required artifacts. I'll send pricing, SOC2/VPC/KMS docs. Olivia will give sample dataset counts. Then we'll schedule a technical deep dive for index architecture.
07:00 Speaker 2 (Rajat): Thanks, appreciate it.
07:03 Speaker 1 (Maya): Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email with the materials.
